23_marg442: By the names of places the regions of the nations are noted. For as the cosmographers write: 'From the river Indus, which is on the east, to the Tigris, which is on the west, these are the regions: Aracusia, Parthia, Assyria, Persis and Media, mountainous and rugged. On the north they have mount Caucasus, on the south the Red Sea and the Persian gulf. In their midst are the chief rivers Hydaspes and Ardinus. In these are twenty-two nations; but in general it is often called Parthia, and Media [so the edition]. From the Tigris to the Euphrates is Mesopotamia, beginning from the north between mount Taurus and the Caucasus; to which on the south succeeds Babylonia, then Chaldea, lastly Arabia, which stretches toward the east in a narrow tract of land between the Persian and the Arabian [gulfs]. In these are twenty-two nations.' And so it came about that two most powerful kingdoms, fighting each other, procured very many nations from their borders, and at last the victories went to the Chaldeans or Assyrians.
23_marg443: When the devil subjects the multitude of the lost to his will, his heart is lifted up, assigning it to his own power and not to divine permission; and he burns the more for the destruction of very many lost ones, the more he sees himself prevail over some by wicked suggestion. 23_marg444: AND HE SENT etc. The devil sends envoys through the various provinces when he scatters the crowd of evil spirits through the whole world to seduce the nations. He spares neither dignity nor honor; he desires to drag all to hell and to make them children of perdition. He does not suffer even the faithful, who are signified by the names of Jerusalem and Jordan, to be secure; nor is it enough for him to swallow up the heathen unless he can also devour Christians. Hence Job: 'He will drink up a river and not wonder, and he trusteth that the Jordan may run into his mouth.' And again: 'His meat is choice.' But although he overcomes many, he is despised by many. Hence: They all with one mind refused.

23_marg453: THEN ACHIOR. As it were a prince of the heretics, any one given to idolatry, who has known of the divine works and miracles, which he often tells to others, although he has not perfectly learned the catholic faith and has not been reborn in the baptism of Christ. Or by Achior heretics are designated, who, although they do not hold the way of truth in all things, yet in their doctrine preach many true things which agree with our faith. These fight against the catholic Church, but, overcome by reason, do not altogether hide the truth. For heretics mingle good with evil, because if they always spoke evil they could not lie hid; as he who offers a cup of poison touches the lip of the cup with honey, that what is sweet may be perceived first, lest what is deadly be feared. Sometimes, however, being corrected, they are saved; as Achior, seeing the victory of Judith, being joined to the people of God, circumcised the flesh of his foreskin. The lepers of the gospel also express the heretics, who, while they insert wrong things among right, as it were sprinkle a healthy color with spots.

For the devil strives most for this: to take away the streams of doctrine and the arms of virtues, and so swiftly to accomplish his wickedness unto the destruction of the servants of God. Hence the princes of the gentiles and Julian the apostate forbade Christians not only divine but also human philosophy.

23_marg459: AND THESE FIVE DAYS. The five days are the five senses of the body, by which the present life is led. The idle doctor asks as it were a truce of five days, who indiscreetly promises his hearers comfort for bodily vitium [so the edition], as if the magnificence of the supreme giver were in his power, whereas the time and manner of giving rest rather in the power of the giver than of the receiver. For if the comfort of the present life is denied, they desert their subjects, so that by yielding to persecutions they may avoid bodily punishment. This agreement our Judith, that is, the Church, rejects and despises.

23_marg460: Daughter of Merari, that is, of bitterness. For the Church through bitterness and tribulation is begotten to the joys of the future life, where it will praise the Lord for ever. That she is related to have been born in the fifteenth generation signifies that the Church was brought forth from the patriarchs and apostles through the seven of the law and the eight of the gospel, and is to ascend to heavenly grace. Hence this number of steps is set in the psalter, figurative of the future ascension to heaven, at which the saints, coming, rightly say: 'Behold now bless ye.'
23_marg461: AND HER HUSBAND MANASSES. Manasses is interpreted 'forgetful' or 'necessity'; joined to whom in wedlock Judith was as it were bound to the decalogue of the law or to the rites of the gentiles; but when Christ came and the light of the gospel shone in the world, all that observance gave way and, like a cheap gathering of harvest, swiftly passed. Hence the Apostle: 'After the faith is come, we are no longer under a pedagogue. For you are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.' And to the Romans he says: 'You also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ Jesus, that you may belong to another, who is risen again from the dead.'
23_marg462: Manasses is Christ, the bridegroom of the Church. He is well called Manasses, because he makes us forget our former calamity through the consolation of the future life. He came in the time of the barley harvest, that is, of the gathering of the Jewish people, when he sent his apostles to preach and to gather the sheaves of believers. The heat of persecution [came] upon his head, that is, upon his divinity; for the head of Christ is God. For the Jews were most scandalized at this, that he said he was the Son of God. Hence: 'Thou makest thyself God.' And elsewhere: 'Because he made himself the Son of God.' Jesus suffered among his own nation and was buried in a garden. His bride, the bridegroom being taken away, gives herself to fasting and prayer until the consummation of the world, and does not deign to be polluted with heretical errors; to whom her husband left the riches of spiritual wisdom and virtue, and gathered a household, that is, the multitude of the gentiles.

23_marg490: AND ACHIOR SEEING. By Achior, the prince of the Ammonites, pagans or heretics are designated, who, seeing that the faith of the Church has overcome the ferocity of the enemies, are struck with exceeding fear, and humbling their pride venerate the Church, and exhort their followers to leave their error and to join themselves to the faithful. Hence Isaias: 'The children of them that afflicted thee shall come bowing down to thee, and all that slandered thee shall worship the steps of thy feet.'

23_marg491: THEN VAGAO GOING IN. The leaders of the persecutors, asking help of their gods against the Church, find them most filthy with their own foulness and destitute of all power; whereupon, committing themselves to flight, they leave the things in which they trusted for a time: 'For there is no wisdom, there is no prudence, there is no counsel against the Lord.' Hence Jeremias says: 'Let not the swift flee away, nor the strong think to escape', etc.
23_marg492: SO THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SEEING. 23_marg499: ADONAI LORD etc. One of the ten names among the Hebrews, signifying that the Lord rules over creation. And it is to be noted that wherever 'Lord' is set twice, the first name is the tetragrammaton, belongs properly to God and is called ineffable; the second is the common one, which befits men. And well is the Son of God called Adonai Lord, because he is God and man, Lord and God, in that he rules over all or is feared by all.
